३७६
*
श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता
*
[ अध्याय ५
विशेषण है; परन्तु इन्द्रियोंसे ही ममता हटानेके लिये कहा | परन्तु शरीर, मन, बुद्धि, इन्द्रियोंके द्वारा किसीका अभीष्ट
हो गया, किसीकी मनचाही बात हो गयी - इन क्रियाओंको
लेकर अपने मनमें खुशी आती है तो मन, बुद्धि आदिमें
केवलपना नहीं रहा, प्रत्युत उनके साथ सम्बन्ध जुड़ गया,
ममता हो गयी।
जाय, शरीर-मन-बुद्धिसे नहीं - ऐसा सम्भव नहीं है ।
शरीरादिका सम्बन्ध समष्टि संसारके साथ है । व्यष्टि कभी
समष्टिसे अलग नहीं हो सकती। इसलिये व्यष्टि -
(शरीरादि-) से सम्बन्ध जोड़नेपर समष्टि - (संसार - ) से
स्वतः सम्बन्ध जुड़ जाता है । जैसे लड़कीसे विवाह होनेपर
अर्थात् सम्बन्ध जुड़नेपर सास, ससुर आदि ससुरालके सभी
सम्बन्धियोंसे अपने-आप सम्बन्ध जुड़ जाता है, ऐसे ही
संसारकी किसी भी वस्तु - (शरीरादि - ) से सम्बन्ध जुड़नेपर
अर्थात् उसे अपनी माननेपर पूरे संसारसे अपने-आप
सम्बन्ध जुड़ जाता है। अतः यहाँ 'केवलैः ' पद शरीर -
इन्द्रियाँ -मन-बुद्धि सबमें ही साधकको ममता हटानेकी
प्रेरणा करता है ।
वास्तवमें कर्ताका स्वयं निर्मम होना ही आवश्यक है ।
यदि कर्ता स्वयं निर्मम हो तो शरीर, इन्द्रियाँ, मन, बुद्धि
आदि सब जगहसे ममता सर्वथा मिट जाती है । कारण कि
वास्तवमें शरीर, इन्द्रियाँ आदि स्वरूपसे सर्वथा भिन्न हैं;
अतः इनमें ममता केवल मानी हुई है, वास्तवमें है नहीं ।
कर्मयोगकी साधनामें फलकी इच्छाका त्याग मुख्य है
(गीता–पाँचवें अध्यायका बारहवाँ श्लोक) । साधारण
लोग फलप्राप्तिके लिये कर्म करते हैं, पर कर्मयोगी
फलकी आसक्तिको मिटानेके लिये कर्म करता है । परन्तु
जो शरीर, इन्द्रियाँ, मन, बुद्धि, प्राण आदिको अपना मानता
रहता है, वह फलकी इच्छाका त्याग कर ही नहीं सकता ।
कारण कि उसका ऐसा भाव रहता है कि शरीरादि अपने
हैं तो उनके द्वारा किये गये कर्मोंका फल भी अपनेको
मिलना चाहिये । इस प्रकार शरीरादिको अपना माननेसे
स्वतः फलकी इच्छा उत्पन्न होती है। इसलिये फलकी
इच्छाको मिटानेके लिये शरीरादिको कभी भी अपना न
मानना अत्यन्त आवश्यक है।
,
-
'केवलैः' - पदका तात्पर्य है कि जैसे वर्षा बरसती
है और उससे लोगोंका हित होता है; परन्तु उसमें ऐसा
भाव नहीं होता कि मैं बरसती हूँ, मेरी वर्षा है जिससे
-
‘सङ्गं त्यक्त्वात्मशुद्धये' – [ पीछे दसवें श्लोकमें भी
'सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा' पद आये हैं; अतः इनकी व्याख्या वहीं
देखनी चाहिये । ]
साधारणतः मल, विक्षेप और आवरण-दोषके दूर
होनेको अन्तःकरणकी शुद्धि माना जाता है । परन्तु वास्तवमें
अन्तःकरणकी शुद्धि है - शरीर - इन्द्रियाँ - मन-बुद्धिसे ममताका
सर्वथा मिट जाना । शरीरादि कभी नहीं कहते कि हम
तुम्हारे हैं और तुम हमारे हो। हम ही उनको अपना मान
लेते हैं । उनको अपना मानना ही अशुद्धि है— ' ममता मल
जरि जाइ' (मानस ७ । ११७ क) । अतः शरीरादिके प्रति
अहंता - ममतापूर्वक माने गये सम्बन्धका सर्वथा अभाव ही
आत्मशुद्धि है ।
इस श्लोकमें आये 'केवलैः ' पदसे शरीर - इन्द्रियाँ-
मन-बुद्धिको अपना न माननेकी बात आयी है । 'केवलैः
पदमें अपनापन हटानेका उद्देश्य है और 'आत्मशुद्धये '
पदमें अपनापन सर्वथा हटनेकी बात आयी है । तात्पर्य यह
है कि अन्तःकरणकी शुद्धिके लिये (अपनापन सर्वथा
हटानेके उद्देश्यसे) शरीर - इन्द्रियाँ - मन-बुद्धिको अपना न
माननेपर भी इनमें सूक्ष्म अपनापन रह जाता है । उस सूक्ष्म
अपनेपनका सर्वथा मिटना ही आत्मशुद्धि अर्थात् अन्तःकरणकी
शुद्धि है ।
अहंतामें भी ममता रहती है । ममता सर्वथा मिटनेपर
जब अहंतामें भी ममता नहीं रहती, तब सर्वथा शुद्धि हो
जाती है।
'कर्म कुर्वन्ति' – शरीर - इन्द्रियाँ - मन-बुद्धिमें जो सूक्ष्म
अपनापन रह जाता है, उसे सर्वथा दूर करनेके लिये
कर्मयोगी कर्म करते हैं।
जबतक मनुष्य कर्म करते हुए अपने लिये किसी
दूसरोंका हित होगा, दूसरोंको सुख होगा । ऐसे ही इन्द्रियों प्रकारका सुख चाहता है अर्थात् किसी फलकी इच्छा रखता
आदिके द्वारा होनेवाले हितमें भी अपनापन मालूम न दे | | है और शरीर, इन्द्रियाँ, मन आदि कर्म - सामग्रीको अपनी
,
१- यहाँ 'अर्थवशाद् विभक्तिपरिणाम:' के अनुसार 'केवलैः ' पदकी विभक्तिका परिणाम कर लेना चाहिये अर्थात्
'केवलेन कायेन', 'केवलेन मनसा', 'केवलया बुद्ध्या' – इस तरह विभक्तिको बदल लेना चाहिये ।
२- यदि मनुष्य फलकी इच्छा न करे, तो भी शरीरादिको अपना माननेसे वह कर्मफलका हेतु बन ही जाता है, जिसका
भगवान्ने निषेध किया है—' मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भू : ' ( गीता २ । ४७ )।
english:
Here is the translation of the given text:

376

The Shrimad Bhagavad Gita

[Chapter 5]

However, the instructions to remove attachment from the senses have been given. But when one gets a desired result through the body, mind, intellect, and senses, one feels happiness in the mind, and the mind, intellect, etc., do not remain mere spectators; instead, a relationship is established with them, and attachment arises.

Go, do not attach yourself to the body, mind, and intellect - this is not possible. The relationship of the body, etc., is with the collective universe. The individual can never be separate from the collective. Therefore, when a relationship is established with the individual (body, etc.), a relationship is automatically established with the collective (universe). Just as when a girl gets married, i.e., establishes a relationship, she automatically establishes a relationship with her in-laws, etc., similarly, when a relationship is established with any object of the universe (body, etc.), one automatically establishes a relationship with the entire universe. Therefore, the word 'kevalaih' (only) in this verse is an instruction to remove attachment from the body, senses, mind, and intellect.

In reality, the doer must be detached. If the doer is detached, then attachment to the body, senses, mind, and intellect is completely eliminated. Because, in reality, the body, senses, etc., are completely different from the doer; therefore, attachment is only an illusion. The main thing in the practice of karma yoga is to renounce the desire for fruit. Ordinary people do karma for the sake of fruit, but the karma yogi does karma to eliminate attachment to fruit. However, he who considers the body, senses, mind, intellect, and life force as his own cannot renounce the desire for fruit. Because, he has the feeling that the body, etc., are his, and therefore, the fruit of the actions done through them should also be his. In this way, considering the body, etc., as one's own generates a desire for fruit. Therefore, it is absolutely necessary to never consider the body, etc., as one's own.

The meaning of the word 'kevalaih' is that just as the rain falls and benefits people, but there is no feeling that 'I am raining' or 'my rain is falling', similarly, when one performs karma, one should not have the feeling that 'I am doing this karma' or 'my karma is being done'.

'Sangam tyaktva atma-shuddhye' - [This phrase has also appeared in the 10th verse; therefore, its explanation should be seen there.]

Ordinarily, the purification of the mind is considered to be the removal of malas, vikshepas, and avaranas. However, in reality, the purification of the mind is the complete elimination of attachment to the body, senses, mind, and intellect. The body, etc., never say, 'We are yours, and you are ours.' We consider them as our own. Considering them as our own is impurity - 'Mamatamala jari jai' (Manas 7.117).

Therefore, the complete absence of attachment to the body, etc., is the purification of the mind.

In this verse, the phrase 'kevalaih' has come, which means not to consider the body, senses, mind, and intellect as one's own. The word 'kevalaih' has the intention of removing attachment, and the phrase 'atma-shuddhye' means the complete elimination of attachment. The meaning is that when one does not consider the body, senses, mind, and intellect as one's own for the sake of the purification of the mind (i.e., to eliminate attachment), even then, a subtle attachment remains. The complete elimination of that subtle attachment is the purification of the mind.

Attachment remains in ahanta (I-ness). When attachment is completely eliminated, then ahanta is also completely pure.

'Karman kurvanti' - The subtle attachment that remains in the body, senses, mind, and intellect is completely eliminated by the karma yogi through karma.

As long as a person performs karma, he should not have the feeling that he is doing it for his own benefit or that it will benefit others. He should not have the feeling that he is doing it for the sake of pleasure or that it will bring pleasure to others. He should not have the feeling that he is doing it for the sake of happiness or that it will bring happiness to others. He should not have the feeling that he is doing it for the sake of his own benefit or that it will benefit others.

1. Here, the result of the word 'kevalaih' should be changed according to the rule of 'artha-vashad vibhakti-parinama', i.e., it should be changed to 'kevalena kayena', 'kevalena manasa', 'kevalaya buddhya', etc.

2. Even if a person does not have a desire for fruit, he becomes a cause for the fruit of karma by considering the body, etc., as his own, which is prohibited by the Lord - 'Ma karma-phala-heturbhuh' (Gita 2.47).
